subject: Hospitality
title: The 28-Square-Meter Standard
description: A short lesson to help you apply The 28-Square-Meter Standard.

hook.text: The average hotel room worldwide is about 28 square meters. That number hasn't changed much in decades.

buildup.text: A 28 sqm room must fit a king bed, desk, closet, bathroom, and seating. Every centimeter is planned by specialized architects.

discovery.text: Designers test room layouts with mock-ups. They watch guests navigate the space.

twist.text: Micro-hotels like Yotel offer rooms as small as 10 sqm—proving that clever design can make tiny spaces feel comfortable.

climax.text: Room size matters less than room design. A well-designed 20 sqm room can feel more spacious than a poorly designed 35 sqm one.

punchline.text: 28 square meters, endlessly optimized. In hotel rooms, design beats size.

quiz.question: What do micro-hotels like Yotel prove about room design?
options: Clever design can make rooms as small as 10 sqm feel comfortable
Guests don't care about room size
